analysis.title: "No One Can Fill Jensen's Leather Jacket": 14 Banks Weigh In As Wall Street Hunts For Nvidia's Floor After Huang Quits
key_insights: Nvidia announced that co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately and left the board. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while keeping the CFO role. Synopsys veteran Harvey Jones becomes the first board chair. No succession plan was announced.
NVDA was down about 10% premarket to roughly $156, below its 52-week low of $164.27. About $420 billion of market cap was lost before the open and about a third of the company's value in a month.

Scorecard across the 14 notes: three downgrades (Bernstein, KeyBanc, William Blair), six target cuts (Bernstein, JPMorgan, RBC, Cantor, Goldman, Citi) of $60 to $200 each, and mostly Buy ratings otherwise. Thirteen banks still have a target, averaging about $260 (median $250). Seaport is the lone Sell at $180.

All but one note were written before the 8:48am ET announcement and treated the ouster as likely or imminent. Goldman waited for the release. UBS's $300 target was set before the second affair was reported.

Goldman cuts its target to $220 from $300 and keeps Buy. Normalized EPS of $10.00 is unchanged and the multiple falls to 22x from 30x on limited visibility, the management transition and execution risk. It cites Apple after Steve Jobs, when NTM P/E fell from ~17x to ~12x and bottomed near 9x in 2013.

On Goldman's CY27 EPS of $16.70 versus the Street at $15.91, NVDA traded at 9.6x when the note went out. That is near where Apple troughed. Apple took about two years to bottom with a successor in place and no DOJ investigation.

Bernstein's Rasgon downgraded to Market-Perform and halved his target to $200 from $400. He says it is hard to advocate stepping in size because more allegations, investigations and a new CEO variable are likely.

KeyBanc downgraded to Sector Weight, dropped its target and sees fair value at $170 (11x FY28 EPS of $15.54). It describes Huang as chief technology strategist, organizational architect, primary customer interface and public face.

The bull case across Buy-rated notes is that the order book survives the CEO. Piper says NVDA is sold out for CY27 and largely CY28 and that roadmaps for the next two generations are set. Wolfe sees zero fundamental impact through CY28. RBC estimates demand outpaces supply by about 50%.

NVDA trades near 9x to 10x CY27 earnings, which Piper calls a 20-year trough and William Blair a record low. KeyBanc's comp table has the average chip peer at 33x 2027 earnings versus NVDA at 11.2x. RBC calculates a 60% discount to the Mag 7 and 70% to semi peers.
UBS models revenue rising from $216BN to $985BN in FY29 and then falling to $934BN in FY30 and $841BN in FY31. The article notes that forecast was built for a Huang-led company.

The main worry is Nvidia's role as financier of the AI ecosystem. UBS estimates NVDA generates $50-60BN of free cash flow a quarter, much of it recycled to customers, suppliers and neoclouds. A pause could remove $50BN or more from the system while rates are rising and parts of credit are illiquid.

William Blair says existing contracts survive but the next round of deals is at risk, which could let Broadcom and AMD compete harder. Goldman says the same about new multi-party investments at the same scale. Seaport expects the proposed $500 billion neocloud financing platform to fade without Huang.

CoreWeave was down 11% premarket on the day it is marketing a $4BN-plus investment-grade loan. An interim CEO who is also CFO is seen as less likely to sign new backstops, per the JonesTrading comment cited.

Org-chart risk: Wells Fargo says about 60 executives reported directly to Huang and calls that structure not sustainable under a new CEO. Seaport says any internal candidate would be siloed and the company would be competent but less dynamic. Cantor flags talent loss among 42,000 employees and Nvidia's standing at TSMC.

Candidates named: Ian Buck (Piper, others), Jonathan Ross (William Blair), Jeff Fisher, Debora Shoquist and Bill Dally (RBC). Outside names floated to Bloomberg are Lisa Su, Rene Haas and Sanjay Mehrotra. Wells, Piper and Cantor correctly guessed Kress as interim.
Wedbush's precedents (Marvell, Apple under Cook, HP, Intel) do not fit. It cannot recall a case combining a founder-driven company, central importance to tech policy and no apparent succession plan.

Regulatory overhang continues. A board investigation under Wachtell's Joon Kim is ongoing, the DOJ holds the Megaspeed probe, the House wants a closed-door briefing on Nov 18, Senators Warren and Coons want records, and Beijing says Washington is using the affair to justify a chip blockade.

Banks differ on China and export exposure. JPMorgan removed the 'China + Other' bucket (about 8% of first-half revenue) from FY28 and cut FY28 EPS about 9% to $14.45. UBS puts about 10% of revenue at risk. Wolfe and RBC call the China line tiny (RBC: about 1% of data center revenue, excluded from guidance).

Beneficiaries named by BNP, Seaport and William Blair are AMD and Broadcom. BNP adds Arista and Celestica if networking unbundles from GPUs and says lower Nvidia HBM buying could ease memory pricing. Wedbush names AMD and Cerebras. William Blair argues coding agents are eroding CUDA lock-in.

Four banks cluster on a $150 floor: Cantor at 9x CY27 EPS, Piper at its 10x trough multiple, KeyBanc's bear case and Citi's bear case at 11x. RBC's downside case is $100 at 6x CY27 EPS. Goldman declined to name a floor.
At about $156 premarket NVDA is about 4% above the consensus floor. The article expects the floor to be tested and sides with Rasgon's caution over the low multiple.

Upcoming: Kress presents Q3 results on Nov 17, the day before the House closed-door briefing on Nov 18. Seaport expects 2027 AI spending to hold and 2028 to be tougher, with an Anthropic IPO possibly coming next week.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman (Schneider) cut the target from $300 and kept Buy. Normalized EPS of $10.00 is unchanged and the multiple falls to 22x from 30x on the leadership transition.
Bernstein (Rasgon) moved to Market-Perform and cut the target from $400. He expects more allegations and investigations and does not advocate buying in size.
KeyBanc (Vinh) cut to Sector Weight from Overweight and dropped the target. Fair value is $170, or 11x FY28 EPS of $15.54.
William Blair (Naji) moved to Market Perform. It worries about deals Huang will not make and a shrinking moat as coding agents lower CUDA switching costs.
JPMorgan (Sur) cut the target from $320. It removed the China + Other bucket from FY28 and cut FY28 EPS about 9% to $14.45.
RBC (Pajjuri) cut the target from $330. It sees demand about 50% above supply and a downside case of $100 at 6x CY27 EPS.
Citi (Malik) cut the target from $285 in a note titled 'Nvidia Without Jensen? Lowering Target Price Again'. Its bear case is $150 at 11x.
Cantor (Muse) cut the target from $350 and removed NVDA from its Top Pick list. It sees 9x CY27 EPS, or $150, as about right and expects consensus to assume lower share and margins.
Piper Sandler (O'Connor) sees roadmaps for the next two generations as set and the company sold out for CY27 and largely CY28. It sees $150 as the floor on a 10x trough multiple.
Wolfe (Caso) sees no impact on fundamentals or earnings through at least CY28 and calls export worries misplaced. It has the stock under 8x its FY29 earnings power view.
Wedbush (Bryson) notes four straight beats of more than 5% on average and expects the 70% revenue growth outlook for next year to be lifted. It says uncertainty is already in the price.
BNP Paribas (Ackerman) keeps Outperform. It flags possible strain with TSMC and expects more scrutiny to cut GPU exports to China and Taiwan.
UBS (Arcuri) kept Buy and $300 in a note published Wednesday night. It lists Nvidia's role as funder of AI ecosystem participants as the first key area of impact.
Seaport (Goldberg) is the lone Sell and the target is under review. He expects the $500 billion financing platform to fade and 2028 AI spending to become tougher.
Wells Fargo (Quatrochi) calls a structure with about 60 direct reports to the CEO not sustainable under a new CEO. It says the fate of Nvidia's investments and backstops is unknown.

sector_views.rationale: Seaport and JonesTrading expect a new CEO to write fewer backstop checks than Huang. CoreWeave fell 11% premarket while marketing a $4BN-plus loan.
BNP, Seaport and William Blair name AMD and Broadcom as winners as customers diversify. BNP sees custom chips approaching three-quarters of AI accelerator units by 2030.

earnings_insights: Goldman estimate: normalized EPS of $10.00 unchanged (basis for the $220 target at 22x). Goldman CY27 EPS estimate is $16.70 versus Street consensus of $15.91.
KeyBanc estimate: FY28 EPS of $15.54, with fair value at 11x. JPMorgan estimate: FY28 EPS cut about 9% to $14.45 after removing the China + Other bucket, about 8% of first-half revenue.
UBS estimate (not reported): revenue of $216BN last fiscal year rising to $985BN in FY29, then $934BN in FY30 and $841BN in FY31.
Wedbush: Nvidia has beaten by more than 5% on average in each of the last four quarters. It expects the company to lift its 70% revenue growth outlook for next year (forecast).

RBC: China was about 1% of data center revenue last quarter and is excluded from guidance. Goldman cites the FY26 10-K showing 11% of sales to mainland China, Hong Kong and other regions outside the US and Taiwan.
Nvidia is scheduled to present Q3 results on Nov 17 with Kress as interim CEO and CFO. No consensus figures for that print are given.

trade_ideas.description: Long NVDA as a long-term buying opportunity at 9-10x earnings (Piper Sandler view)
trade_ideas.rationale: Piper says the order book is sold out through CY28 and the multiple is a 20-year trough.
trade_ideas.risk: Rasgon warns more allegations and investigations are likely and the CEO successor is unknown.

risk_factors: More allegations or investigations surfacing, per Bernstein's 'two ants in the kitchen' argument.
No succession plan and an interim CEO who is also CFO. About 60 direct reports to the departed CEO.
Pause in Nvidia's funding of neoclouds, LLM developers and suppliers, estimated at $50BN or more out of the ecosystem.
Failure of the proposed $500 billion financing platform to finalize.
Tighter export rules or scrutiny covering Singapore, Malaysia and China.
Strain with TSMC and loss of talent.
Market share loss to AMD, Broadcom and custom silicon, and erosion of CUDA lock-in.
Out-year revenue in UBS's model declining in FY30 and FY31.
Multiple compression to RBC's 6x CY27 EPS downside case.
charts_described: Bernstein price target history chart: the target went to $400 as recently as Aug 27 before the cut to $200 (source: Bernstein).
Goldman chart of Apple's forward P/E around Steve Jobs' leave and death: ~17x to ~12x, troughing near 9x in 2013, recovering to ~15x.
Citi chart supporting a $150 bear case at 11x.
KeyBanc comp table: average chip peer at 33x 2027 earnings, median 31x, Nvidia at 11.2x.
vol_and_positioning: NVDA is down about 10% premarket at roughly $156, versus a 52-week low of $164.27 and about 4% above the Street's consensus floor of $150.
At Wednesday's close NVDA traded at about 10x CY27 earnings, now 9x to 10x. KeyBanc shows chip peers at 33x average and 31x median versus NVDA at 11.2x.
CoreWeave is down 11% premarket. Cantor, Piper, KeyBanc and Citi put the floor at $150. RBC's downside case is $100.
geopolitical: The board's independent investigation led by Wachtell's Joon Kim continues. The DOJ holds the Megaspeed probe and has looked at customers' shipments through Singapore.
The House wants a closed-door briefing on Nov 18. Senators Warren and Coons are demanding records.
Beijing accuses Washington of using the affair to justify a chip blockade. Cantor calls the resignation a 'W' for China in the AI race.
Banks expect more export scrutiny of Singapore, Malaysia, Southeast Asian and sovereign buyers. William Blair raises a possible revival of diffusion-style country caps or broader entity listings.

tension_points.bull_case: Order book is sold out through CY27 and largely CY28 per Piper, Wolfe and RBC. At 9x to 10x CY27 EPS the multiple is at a 20-year trough, and Wedbush argues uncertainty is already priced.
tension_points.bear_case: Every floor assumes earnings hold, but earnings rest on Huang's relationships and Nvidia's vendor financing. Four banks cluster at $150 and the article expects it to be tested. Rasgon expects more allegations. Apple took about two years to bottom.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below the $150 level that Cantor, Piper, KeyBanc and Citi use as a floor, with RBC's $100 case at 6x CY27 EPS as the next marker.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman expects every announced commitment to be honored, and existing contracts survive a CEO change per William Blair.
tension_points.bear_case: New backstops and investments at the same scale get harder. UBS sees a possible pause removing $50BN or more from the ecosystem and Seaport expects the $500 billion platform to fade.

tension_points.bull_case: Wolfe says AI shipments to China are already de minimis. RBC says China is about 1% of data center revenue and excluded from guidance.
tension_points.bear_case: JPMorgan removed about 8% of first-half revenue from FY28. UBS puts about 10% of revenue at risk, with Singapore and Malaysia exposure not booked as China.
